questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'The flood _______ many buildings in the coastal town last year.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. AFFECT (verb) = to have an impact on something. EFFECT (verb) = to bring about/accomplish (e.g., 'effect a change'). 'The flood affected buildings' = had a damaging impact on them.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'The manager gave _______ tickets to his staff for the annual concert.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. COMPLIMENTARY = given free as a gesture of goodwill, or expressing praise. COMPLEMENTARY = completing or enhancing something else. Tickets given as a gift = complimentary.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'She _______ the entire report carefully before submitting it for review.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. PERUSE = to read or examine carefully and thoroughly. PURSUE = to chase or follow. PERSUADE = to convince. PERVADE = to spread through.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'The _______ of the accused was established beyond reasonable doubt by the prosecution.'
questions.explanation: D is correct. GUILT = the fact of having committed an offence. GUILE = cunning deceit. GULL = to deceive/a seabird. GUILELESS = innocent, without deception.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'The minister _______ a bold plan to modernise the entire judicial system.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. ENVISAGE = to imagine or conceive of a future possibility. ENACT = to make into law. ENFORCE = to compel compliance. 'Envisaged a bold plan' = conceived/visualised the plan.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'His _______ to detail was what set his work apart from his colleagues.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. ATTENTION TO DETAIL is the standard collocation meaning careful observation. INTENTION = a plan or aim. CONTENTION = a point of dispute. DETENTION = confinement/delay.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'She was _______ to her mother's advice and stubbornly refused to follow it.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. AVERSE = having a strong dislike or reluctance (averse to advice). ADVERSE = harmful or unfavourable (adverse conditions). AVERRED = declared/stated firmly. AVERTED = turned away/prevented.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'The new traffic regulations will directly _______ the lives of millions of commuters.'
questions.explanation: D is correct. AFFECT (verb) = to have an impact on. 'Affect the lives of commuters' = impact them. EFFECT as a verb means 'to bring about a change' and does not fit this structure.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'His _______ arguments seemed convincing at first but completely collapsed under close scrutiny.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. SPECIOUS = apparently sound or valid but actually wrong or deceptive. The clue is 'seemed convincing at first but collapsed' — exactly what specious means. SPACIOUS = having ample space.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'A truly _______ historian presents events without personal bias or hidden agenda.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. DISINTERESTED = impartial, having no personal stake in the outcome. UNINTERESTED = not interested, bored. A historian presenting events fairly = disinterested (impartial), not uninterested (bored).
